og_title: The Crimson Flame of Karma and the Empty Sky

twitter_description: Karmic Hellfire tests Ji Ning's soul. The Shaoyin Ancestor banishes him from the Three Realms. A shocking volume end for Desolate Era.

lore_anchors.definition: A formless, divine flame that punishes a cultivator for their karmic sin by burning the soul and testing the Dao-heart, bypassing all physical defenses.
A supremely powerful Innate Spirit treasure of the Shaoyin clan, capable of banishing a target across dimensions and even out of the Three Realms.
A classification of magic treasure below an Immortal-ranked treasure but still incredibly powerful, suitable for suppressing lesser enemies or holding items.
Periodic, unavoidable ordeals that plague all cultivators below the Celestial Immortal stage, increasing in intensity over time and serving as a crucible for the Dao-heart.
The core of a cultivator's mental and spiritual resolve; the unshakable will that governs their path. A strong Dao-heart is essential for resisting soul attacks and mental tribulations.
A legendary treasure born from the primordial chaos or the very fabric of the universe, possessing innate power and often sentience, making them far superior to man-made treasures.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn't Ji Ning teleport away at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The hellfire had reduced his rationality to an extremely low, animalistic level. He was only capable of instinctive defense (striking at threats) and could no longer process complex tactics like escape.

No. He was banished outside the Three Realms by the Realm-Refining Tower. This is a classic Xianxia cliffhanger used to force a protagonist into a new, even more dangerous, and power-boosting territory.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the hellfire treating Ji Ning and the Scourgewind Fiend-Demon differently?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Scourgewind Fiend-Demon's Dao-heart is more refined due to surviving a million years of tribulations. Ji Ning's raw resolve is immense but unseasoned, making the same pain feel much more overwhelming to him.
